name: Yama

mechanics.name: Axe Swing
mechanics.description: He swings his axe at whoever is next to him, and it catches everyone within three tiles of that target rather than just them.
mechanics.counterplay: Pray Protect from Melee before it lands and it drops from crushing to trivial.

mechanics.name: Fire and Shadow
mechanics.description: Flames or shadowy swirls gather on you, then he snaps his fingers. Flames are magic, shadows are ranged, and the swirl tells you which is coming.
mechanics.counterplay: Read the effect around your character and set your overhead before the snap. Getting it right blocks it entirely.

mechanics.name: Glyphs of Fire and Shadow
mechanics.description: Two glyphs sit near the throne. Standing on one blocks the matching kind of damage, and how much they hurt or drain depends on how close he is.
mechanics.counterplay: Step onto the glyph matching whatever special he is about to use. Fire glyph for fire, shadow glyph for the prayer drain.

mechanics.name: Stomp
mechanics.description: He stamps and the floor answers, dropping rock and shadow across the arena.
mechanics.counterplay: Watch where the tremors mark and get off those tiles.

mechanics.name: Void Flares
mechanics.description: Demonic orbs appear with a charging bar. When the bar fills they burst for very heavy damage.
mechanics.counterplay: Destroy them before the bar fills, or stand on the glyph matching their colour so the burst does nothing.

mechanics.name: Judge of Yama
mechanics.description: At two thirds and one third health he sends you across the lava to fight the Judge. It holds two protection prayers at once, starting on melee and ranged and then following whatever you last hit it with.
mechanics.counterplay: Bring magic. It is the one style the Judge cannot cover from the start, and hopping stones is how you cross.

_note: SKELETON, NOT LIVE-VERIFIED. Ids come from Jagex's own gameval names rather than guesses, but nothing here has been confirmed in a live fight. Provenance: gamevals from runelite-api 1.12.35 (net.runelite.api.gameval.*), because this cache download ships an empty GAMEVALS index (idx24) and ScanGameVal cannot read it; npc names, models, sequences and extents from the live cache (revision of 2026-08-06). Npc ids 14176, 15555 and 15700 are the boss, all carrying models [10468, 10338, 10340] and standing animation 12140. Several other npcs share the name and are excluded: YAMA_THRONE 123 and YAMA_THRONE_OCCUPIED 124 are furniture, 15645 and 14157 are the throne scene, and the Voice and Disciple npcs are dialogue. The Judge is AKD_JUDGE_OF_YAMA_COMBAT 10938 with 14180 and 15663; all three are curated as npc-spawn triggers because it is not established which the fight uses. Animations are the NPC_YAMA01_* set, all unambiguous gameval names: IDLE 12140, MAGIC01 12144, MAGIC02 12145, MELEE01 12146, PORTAL01 12147 and STOMP01 12148. THE TWO MAGIC SEQUENCES ARE CURATED AS ONE MECHANIC covering both fire and shadow, because the wiki describes them as the same move differing only in which effect gathers on you, and the cache offers no way to tell which sequence is which. Projectiles VFX_PROJ_YAMA_FIRE_SKULL_01 12102, VFX_YAMA_FLAMING_ROCK_PROJECTILE_01 12105 and VFX_YAMA_SHADOW_SPIKE_PROJECTILE_01 12108 are curated because each says projectile outright in Jagex's own name; the matching SPOTANIM and IMPACT ids (12095 through 12101, 12104, 12106, 12107, 12109, 12110) are graphics and are left out, since a graphic trigger has no source actor to check (docs/DECISIONS.md D17) and discovery never revokes (D18). The whole fight is laid out under a YAMA_ prefix in the gamevals, which is what gives three of these mechanics exact npc triggers: YAMA_VOIDFLARE 14179 is the flare, YAMA_METEOR_NPC 14182 is what the stomp drops, and YAMA_JUDGE_OF_YAMA 14180 is the Judge. YAMA_IMP 14181 exists and is deliberately not curated, because the wiki's mechanic list has nothing matching it. THE GLYPH MECHANIC DETECTS ON PORTAL01 12147, which is an inference: the glyphs are ground markers rather than anything the boss animates, and the portal sequence is the closest thing in his set. It is the weakest trigger in this file. THIS BOSS'S ANIMATIONS ARE SKELETAL, SO THE PREVIEW VALUES ARE AN ESTIMATE, NOT ARITHMETIC (docs/DECISIONS.md D36). FitZoom returned empty extents for all three sequences tried. The values follow the method Doom of Mokhaiotl already ships under: take the zoom from struct 4737, the Combat Achievements screen's own entry, which pins model 10339 at zoom 2500, and compute shiftY from the bind pose extents at that zoom. THE PREVIEW PINS modelId 10339 RATHER THAN RESOLVING THROUGH npcId, and here that is not merely preferable but necessary: 10339 is not in the npc's model list at all (which holds 10468, 10338 and 10340), so it is a merged model built for the CA screen, exactly the case that produced the half-rendered General Graardor fixed in issue #89. The Judge preview resolves through npcId and borrows the generic DEMON_UPDATE_* set the way Skotizo does. staticFallback is false on all six; whether each body animation reads has not been eyeballed in game, and for a skeletal boss that check matters more than usual. The collection log page is titled 'Yama', matching 'name'.
